page: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is an x86_64 architecture virtual server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that this instance operates in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the server in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. While cached memory bandwidth achieves average speeds of 367.64 GB/sec, uncached read and write memory bandwidth drops to the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and compression tasks, including gzip and bzip3, also register weak to poor throughput.

This server utilizes a shared CPU allocation model, which introduces potential resource contention tradeoffs but offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for non-critical workloads. The inclusion of 160 GB of fast NVMe SSD storage provides a solid storage-to-compute ratio for budget-conscious deployments, though memory-intensive operations like Redis SET and database transactions are constrained by the lower memory performance tier.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is best suited for lightweight applications. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, software development and testing environments, small utility scripts, and basic staging environments where continuous high-performance compute is not required.
